review_conclusions: The formal pages accurately state the held-slot passive reads the target native stagger.count at each applicable generic damage calculation, without a kill, positive-HP-damage, or newly-caused-stagger gate. The attack reads the pre-damage count; stagger added later in that attack cannot retroactively change the same calculation.

All eight actual implementations share own I–IV per-count values .14/.16/.18/.20, replacing the base same-key fallback .5. With the additive-multiplier stat neutral at 1, the damage consumer contributes p×clamp(count,0,7) to the additive damage-stat pool. The tier page and examples correctly keep this coefficient-stage amount separate from final HP damage.

The controlled examples state their assumptions and arithmetic: IV, count 4, B=100 gives coefficient 1→1.8 and intermediate output 100→180; with q=.30 the comparison is 130→210 (80 points, about 61.54% relative); count 7 gives +140 percentage points at IV. These are not final health-damage percentages.

The English RAW explicitly says “Up to” the formatted tier percentage, while the fixed-source consumer at IV/count 7 adds 1.40 to the damage-stat pool; the formal erratum correctly identifies that cap contradiction. The Traditional Chinese RAW omits the per-count formula and cap, so it is correctly classified as not covered rather than contradictory.

The player page and all variant pages distinguish the actual 18 Marks and their routed hitscan, pellet, charged, arc, Sweep and special attack paths. Pellet groups are not treated as one event per pellet; the actual burning tick is a separate damage call. The shield push has zero base health damage and does not create damage from this additive pool.

The candidate preview snapshot and current shared blessing map are exactly equal for all eight trait variants and 18 bindings. The image receipt uses icon 115, separate icon path and attachment URL, and records verified public bytes and display.
